system.deviceRole: Central-count ballot scanning and tabulation system
system.summary: A separate source-linked dossier for the ImageCast Central configuration: a certified COTS high-speed scanner, workstation, ICC application, removable-media accessories, optional isolated network infrastructure, and documented backup power.

certification.caveat: EAC certification applies only to the evaluated Democracy Suite 5.17 certified configuration. It does not establish which scanner or workstation alternative a jurisdiction selected, the condition of a field unit, or an installation's network configuration.

components.name: Central-count COTS scanner
components.description: ImageCast Central pairs one supported commercial high-speed scanner with the ICC workstation and ballot-processing application.
components.caveat: These are certified alternatives, not components used together. The scene and gallery show representative scanner forms and do not identify the selected model at a jurisdiction.

components.name: ICC client workstation
components.description: The ICC application runs on a certified desktop or all-in-one workstation paired with the selected scanner.
components.caveat: Workstation alternatives vary by scanner configuration. The certification documents do not establish which processor, memory, storage, display, or connector occupation exists in a particular installation.

technicalSpecifications.label: Certified workstation operating system
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is the evaluated operating-system platform, not a live patch-level reading or evidence for a particular field workstation.

components.name: ImageCast Central application
components.description: The proprietary ICC application controls ballot image capture, interpretation, batch acceptance, and central-count tabulation.
components.caveat: The certified version is not a live field reading. The schematic screen is symbolic and does not reproduce a proprietary user interface.

technicalSpecifications.label: Certified ICC application
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is the application version in the final certified configuration, not a field-observed installation or a claim that it is the newest later release.

components.name: iButton reader and adapter
components.description: Certified auxiliary hardware includes the Dallas Maxim iButton reader/writer and its 1-Wire USB adapter.
components.caveat: The models are named auxiliary equipment. The source does not establish that the schematic location or cable arrangement matches a particular installation.

components.name: CompactFlash media reader
components.description: Certified auxiliary hardware includes USB CompactFlash reader alternatives used with election media.
modelNumbers: Lexar Professional USB 3.0 Dual-Slot Card Reader
components.caveat: The listed readers are alternatives. Their presence, attached port, and media contents at a particular jurisdiction are not established.

components.name: Optional isolated network infrastructure
components.description: Colorado's 5.17-CO guide calls for high-speed network infrastructure only when an additional central ballot scan repository or data center is used, and requires election computers to remain isolated from the Internet and other networks.
components.caveat: This is a conditional 5.17-CO infrastructure requirement, not evidence that every ICC installation is networked or that any ICC is connected to the Internet.

technicalSpecifications.label: Conditional central-repository network
technicalSpecifications.value: 100 Mbps infrastructure when an additional central repository/data center is used; isolated from the Internet and all other networks
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The guide states a conditional capability and isolation rule. It does not establish cabling, port occupation, enabled services, or field use elsewhere.

components.name: External uninterruptible power supply
components.description: Colorado's 5.17-CO guide identifies an approved APC UPS and a minimum backup duration for the central scanner and workstation.
components.caveat: The guide establishes a Colorado-approved model and minimum operating requirement, not the battery age, health, or actual runtime at a particular site.

versionObservations.label: Certified ICC application
versionObservations.caveat: This is the final certified application version, not a field reading or evidence of a jurisdiction's current installed version.

versionObservations.label: Certified HiPro firmware support
versionObservations.caveat: This version applies only to the InoTec HiPro scanner alternative and is not a firmware claim for the Canon alternatives or a field-observed scanner.

configurationChanges.description: The Pro V&V report records an ICC application update to support InoTec HiPro firmware version 1.0.1074.
configurationChanges.caveat: This is certification configuration history. It does not establish that a jurisdiction selected the HiPro alternative or installed the firmware on a field scanner.

findings.title: No anomalies or deficiencies reported in the 5.17 certification campaign
findings.description: Pro V&V reported no anomalies and no deficiencies during the Democracy Suite 5.17 certification campaign; ICC accuracy and integration testing met the stated requirements.
findings.caveat: A bounded certification-test result is not evidence that every fielded unit is defect-free, and it is not a claim about later versions, operations, misconduct, or election outcomes.

power.runtime: Minimum 15 minutes required by the 5.17-CO guide
power.description: The Colorado guide names the APC SMC1500 and requires enough backup power to complete and save a ballot batch before graceful shutdown.
power.caveat: The minimum is a documented Colorado configuration requirement, not a measured runtime or battery-health observation at a field installation.

networkEvidence.summary: Colorado's exact 5.17-CO technical data connects the ImageCast Central scanner locally to an ICC workstation by USB and describes ICC workstations using a Gigabit Ethernet port on a closed LAN to the EMS data-center network. The ICC user guide makes additional central-repository infrastructure conditional and requires election computers to remain isolated from the Internet and other networks.
networkEvidence.publicationBoundary: This view publishes only the documented system roles, connection media, conditionality, and isolation controls. It omits addressing, credentials, database identifiers, cryptographic keys, switch settings, hostnames, and jurisdiction cable routes.

configurations.title: ICC workstation with conditional closed data-center LAN
configurations.description: A COTS scanner attaches directly to its ICC workstation. Where the additional central ballot-scan repository or data center is used, ICC workstations connect through isolated network infrastructure to EMS storage and services.

nodes.label: ICC central scanner
nodes.details: The certified configuration permits multiple named COTS scanner alternatives.

nodes.label: ICC workstation
nodes.details: The workstation hosts the ICC application and provides the scanner's local computer interface.

nodes.label: Isolated LAN infrastructure
nodes.details: The ICC user guide calls for high-speed network infrastructure only when an additional central repository or data center is used.

nodes.label: EMS data center
nodes.details: The system overview describes the closed LAN as connecting ICC workstations to the EMS data-center network.

links.purpose: Deliver scanner-captured ballot images to the ICC workstation
Connect an ICC workstation to the closed EMS data-center network when the additional repository configuration is used
Store and exchange results and ballot-image data within the election system boundary

controls.label: Internet isolation
controls.description: The 5.17-CO ICC guide requires election computers to be isolated from any Internet connection.

controls.label: Other-network isolation
controls.description: The election computing network must be isolated from jurisdiction computers and networks not used for election operations.

controls.label: Field switch state
controls.description: The selected switch, ports, addressing, and enabled services for any jurisdiction installation are not established here.

configurations.sensitiveDetailsWithheld: No addresses, credentials, keys, database names, hostnames, switch settings, or site-specific network diagrams are collected or displayed.
configurations.caveat: The documents describe permitted 5.17-CO architectures. They do not establish that a particular jurisdiction uses the optional repository, which COTS alternatives it selected, or the live state of a network.

externalPathway.summary: The conditional ICC-to-EMS path is documented only as a closed election LAN. The reviewed Colorado guide requires election computers to remain isolated from the Internet and other networks.
externalPathway.caveat: This classification applies to the reviewed 5.17-CO documentation and does not substitute for a dated inspection of a jurisdiction installation.

gaps.label: Additional repository selection
gaps.description: The reviewed dossier does not establish whether a jurisdiction uses the optional additional central ballot-scan repository or data-center configuration.
gaps.caveat: The module preserves the conditional language instead of forcing one topology onto every ICC installation.

gaps.label: Field-observed network topology
gaps.description: No dated jurisdiction diagram, switch inventory, interface state, or authorized inspection was collected.
gaps.caveat: A documented system architecture is not a live network observation.

caveats: ImageCast Central is a COTS scanner-and-workstation system, not one proprietary enclosure.
Certified scanner and workstation alternatives are listed separately and must not be read as an instruction to combine every option.
The optional network component is conditional and isolated; it is not evidence of Internet connectivity or field use.
The 3D scene is a navigation aid, not a teardown, wiring diagram, exact installation, or unit inventory.
A certification change or test result is not evidence of field occurrence, misconduct, exploitation, or an election outcome effect.

reviewNotes: Approved for feature-gated staging as a separate central-tabulation dossier. Public production activation remains a separate decision.
Added exact 5.17-CO network documentation while retaining the conditional repository and no-field-observation boundaries.
Added source-bounded external-pathway classification so closed networks, physical interfaces, optional transport hardware, and documented routes beyond a local boundary remain visibly distinct.
project_owner: Production publication authorized after source, editorial, build, and browser validation.
